cf.name: Regular Bracket Sequence
cf.why: stack / balance counter keeps only matched brackets

problems.gist: A config linter receives a string s made only of the six bracket characters ( ) [ ] { }. Decide whether the brackets are balanced:

problems.title: Asteroid Collision
problems.gist: You are given an integer array asteroids describing rocks in a row; the index is the rock's position in space from left to right. For each rock, the absolute value is its size and the sign is its direction: positive moves right, negative moves left.

problems.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
problems.gist: You are given an integer array heights. Each value is the height of one bar of a histogram, and every bar has width 1; the bars stand next to each other with no gaps.

problems.title: Daily Temperatures

gfg.why: monotonic stack; return the value, not the distance
monotonic stack looking left instead of right

problems.gist: You get an integer array temperatures, where temperatures[i] is the temperature on day i. Return an array answer of the same length where answer[i] is the number of days you must wait after day i to reach a day that is strictly warmer. If no later day is warmer, answer[i] = 0.

problems.title: Simplify Path
problems.gist: You are given a string path, an absolute Unix-style path (it starts with '/'). Return its simplified canonical path. The input follows these rules:

problems.title: Decode String
problems.gist: A compression tool writes repeated text as k[encoded], meaning the encoded part inside the brackets is repeated exactly k times; k is always a positive integer. Brackets may be nested. Given a compressed string s, return its decoded form.

problems.title: Basic Calculator
problems.gist: You are given a string s holding a valid arithmetic expression. Evaluate it and return the integer result. You must not use any built-in function that evaluates strings as expressions (such as eval()).

problems.title: Online Stock Span
problems.gist: Design a class that reads a stock's daily prices one at a time and, for each new price, returns its span. The span for today is the largest number of consecutive days, ending today and going backwards, on which the price was less than or equal to today's price.

problems.title: Basic Calculator II
problems.gist: You get a string s that holds a valid arithmetic expression. Compute its value and return it as an integer.

problems.title: Minimum Remove to Make Valid Parentheses
problems.gist: A log line s is made of the characters '(', ')' and lowercase English letters. Delete the fewest possible parentheses (at any positions) so that what is left is a valid parentheses string, and return any such result. Letters are never deleted.

problems.title: Next Greater Element I

cc.name: NEXT GREATER ELEMENT
cc.why: next greater for every element (no subset query)

problems.gist: The next greater element of a value x in an array is the first value to the right of x that is strictly bigger than it, or -1 if there is none.
